reasons: Covers the three main backend choices.
Restores environment settings after each test so tests do not affect each other.
Does not check the production Vercel behavior.

terms.meaning: a named value the computer or host provides to the app, such as a database address
a small database kept in a single local file
a hosting service where the app can run

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test file setup
sections.what: Brings in the test tools and the database selection functions and error type.
sections.why: Provides what the tests need to check backend choice.

sections.name: environment
sections.title: Environment restore after each test
sections.what: Remembers the original database address and Vercel flag, and puts them back after each test, then resets the chosen backend.
sections.why: Prevents one test's settings from leaking into another test.
sections.watch_out: If a future test sets a new environment setting, it must also be restored here or it will leak.

sections.name: database backend selection
sections.title: Backend selection checks
sections.what: Three checks: no hosted settings gives local SQLite and a working ping; a Postgres address gives Postgres; Vercel without a database address raises a configuration error.
sections.why: Each check matches one branch of the storage choice.
sections.watch_out: The Postgres check uses a fake placeholder address and never connects, so it does not prove a connection works.

summary: Checks that the database module picks the right storage backend based on environment settings: local SQLite by default, Postgres when a Postgres address is set, and a clear error on Vercel when hosted storage is missing.
purpose: Protects the rule that the app chooses its storage in a predictable way.
why: Likely reason: wrong storage choice would silently lose or misplace data, so each choice is checked.
how: Before each test it saves the relevant environment settings. Each test sets or clears them, resets the chosen backend, asks for a backend, and checks the result. After each test it restores the original settings.
inputs: Environment settings: the database address and the Vercel flag.
outputs: Pass or fail results. The local SQLite test also creates a local database file.
risks: The Vercel test only covers the test mode. The production behavior is not checked here.
debug: If the wrong backend is reported, check the environment values that the test sets, then the selection order in the database module. If the local test fails, check that the data folder can be created.
